title: Google homepage adds AI search sidebar, supports viewing chat history and connecting Gemini notebooks

content_html:
Google is rolling out a new redesign of its homepage, adding a collapsible AI search sidebar that makes it easier for users to view past AI conversations, continue asking questions, and explore web content.

Robby Stein, Google's vice president of product, recently demonstrated this new feature on X. According to a demo video he shared, users can click the gray bar that appears on the left side of the screen to expand the collapsible sidebar. The sidebar will bring together users' search history from AI Mode and offer features such as creating new conversation threads, searching past threads, and connecting to Gemini notebooks.

This change means Google's homepage is evolving further from a traditional search entry point into an AI interaction entry point. Last year, Google integrated the AI Mode button into the search box, allowing users to enter a chatbot-like interactive experience directly from the search page. In May this year, Google upgraded the search box again to support longer queries and added AI-powered autocomplete.

Stein said that users are asking more and more questions when using search, and these questions are often no longer limited to a single query. Google's internal tests found that the sidebar helps users keep moving search tasks forward and further explore online information. Currently, the new homepage experience is being rolled out gradually to desktop users worldwide. This also reflects Google's attempt to integrate traditional keyword search with continuous AI conversations, pushing its search product toward multi-turn interaction and task continuity.
